newsitem.title: USA: McDonnell files shelf for 3.5 mln shares.
newsitem.headline: McDonnell files shelf for 3.5 mln shares.

text.p: McDonnell Douglas Corp filed Wednesday with the Securities and Exchange Commission a shelf registration to sell up to 3.5 million common shares, which include the related stock purchase rights.
The shares are being registered as part of a proposed $14 billion merger McDonnell Douglas and The Boeing Co which first was entered into on December 14, 1996.

The shares being offered are conditional upon approval of the merger by McDonnell Douglas shareholders and the approval of the issuance of Boeing's common shares by the shareholders of Boeing, the filing said.
The McDonnell shares will not be issued unless the company believes that all of the other conditions to the merger pact have been or will be satisfied or waived, where permissible.
Each share of McDonnell common outstanding "immediately prior to the effective time of the merger" will be converted into 1.3 shares of Boeing common stock, the filing said.
The offering will be made through J.P. Morgan & Co.
Net proceeds will be used general corporate purposes. If the merger is consummated, the net proceeds may be used for general corporate purposes of Boeing.
McDonnell Douglas, based in St. Louis, is principally engaged in the research, development and manufacturing of aerospace, commercial and military avionics and defense electronics products.
